speaker: Doctor
text: I'm Dr. Agent. To start, when did this rash first appear, and has it spread or changed in appearance since then? Have you noticed any fever, weight loss, or fatigue accompanying these skin changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text: That raises concern for a systemic condition like vasculitis or an infection triggered by your new arthritis treatment. Could you tell me which specific medications you started for your arthritis, and have you noticed any joint swelling or morning stiffness? Have you also experienced any joint pain, eye redness, or swelling in your fingers or toes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome (DIHS) / DRESS syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with Differential, Liver Function Tests, Eosinophil Count, Serum IgE levels. REQUEST IMAGES: Full body dermatogram showing the rash distribution on the upper back and any associated lymphadenopathy.
